result.early_census_explanation:
**Measured.** q2_early_census removed only 3.0 ms of census at 00 K5 (arm means 106.6 -> 103.6 ms) and 9.4 ms at 00 K10 (516.9 -> 507.5). At raw K5 it removed 13.9 to 17.0 ms against the engine twin at the same frame and K, and 25 to 42 ms at raw K10. The q2 keys make up 35 %, 16 %, 43-46 % and 23-24 % of the keys in those four groups. Each q2 key moved out saves 6.6 to 16 ns of wall time, while the average census cost is 79-82 ns per key at K5 and 89-95 ns at K10. The rest of the lever's chain gain is the tower index, now built on the q2 side (10 ms without ground, 31 ms raw).

**C's error.** At raw K5 C projected -95 to -130 ms, taking the census share of q2 keys to be their key share (0.43-0.46 × 214-232 ms, so -92 to -107 ms of census). The measured lever is about -45 to -48 ms in total: 2-3x too optimistic. On the census alone it is -14 to -17 ms: 6-7x too optimistic.

**Why**, from code and counters:
1. **The census time follows total keys, not traversed keys.** With the lever on, the time after the merge is 74-80 ns per total key, against 79-82 ns with it off. Per late key it is 121-139 ns. The census clock (tower_chain.cpp:1804-1915) still does per-key work on the whole catalogue:
   - `std::vector<tower::BallData> balls(unique)` (1805) value-initialises 224 B per key, q2 keys included, on the main thread (BallData is not trivially default-constructible, ball_data.hpp:24);
   - the early path adds a copy-in of every q2 ball (parallel_ranges, 1837-1843);
   - it adds a serial free of early.balls (1846);
   - the presentations are freed at 1894.

   The only work removed is the parallel, 48-thread traversal of the q2 keys (census_key -> ball_census, 855-870), and the copy and free partly cancel it.
2. **The q2 keys are the cheapest to traverse.** Their balls are diametral balls of accepted close pairs, so they are small. Their shell is regular with exactly 2 sites for 456 695 of the 456 919 at 00 K5, so they skip ShellTable (910). Positivity is trivially true at arity 2 (regular_support_positive returns at line 718). Their key and level are the cheapest to compute. So their share of the ~77 (K5) / ~97 (K10) nodes per key is below their key share. The per-arity node count is not published.
3. **The q2 side's 66-78 ms (168-173 ms raw) is not a measure of q2 traversal.** A fit over 18 cases gives 17.8 ms + 94.0 ns per q2 key (rms 2.0 ms), about the same as the average per-key cost of the full census, even though q2 balls are the smallest. That is consistent with per-key serial work dominating there too: the value-init of early.balls (1045, 224 B per key) plus q2_representatives. The whole q2 side is hidden in any case.

**Size of the serial part: unmeasured, two brackets.**
- If first touch runs at the 6.6 GB/s the device session achieves for its 256 MB and 1.28 GB pinned reservations, value-init is about 44 ms of the ~104 ms census at 00 K5 and ~104 of 229 ms at b02 K5 (35-45 %).
- If it runs at the ~2.5-3 GB/s implied by a fit on bytes alone, it is most of the census.

A local microbenchmark on this loaded codespace, not the G4 VM, shows the operation is heavy: 185-226 ms of thread CPU for 1.31 M BallData, 1.01-1.07 s for 5.5 M, plus 28 ms to free them. Source: `.../scratchpad/r22/attribution/mb/init_bench.cpp`.

**Lever that follows.** Take the per-key serial work out of the census clock: first-touch or value-init the output array on the threads idle during the device calls, or census the q2 keys directly into the final array. Probe v29 needs census sub-timers to size this.

findings.title: 'A systematic plumbing fault is caught' depends on how common the fault is
findings.scenario: The sample is one fixed residue (index 0 mod 64) of key order, not stratified, and it is the same on every run of a given input. A fault that hits m uniformly placed balls escapes with probability about (63/64)^m. Extended shells are 135 to 3542 per frame, so few are sampled: probe_4 has 17124 sampled balls and 17123 declared-support checks, so exactly 1 sampled extended shell. findings.evidence: Comment at full_ball_tower.hpp:199-202 and PROVENANCE ('Une faute systématique est prise par l'échantillon'); R22 probes 0-35 (ext 135-3542 against samp minus dsc of 1-38). Suggest stating the density condition, or rotating the offset with an input digest.

votes.reasoning:
I could not refute this. The mechanism and the numbers hold at f44a8db03.

Code:

- The index is key order (strictly sorted, presorted scan at :1806-1822). Nothing stratifies the sample by arity or shell class.
- So a deterministic fault on m balls escapes on every run of that input with probability about (63/64)^m over placements: about 0.85 at m=10, 0.46 at m=50, 0.21 at m=100 and 0.009 at m=300.
- The finding actually understates one side. A periodic fault that never lands on 0 mod 64 escapes with certainty however dense it is. For example, a fault on every odd index (half the catalogue) or on the last slot of any power-of-two chunk (63 mod 64) would never be seen. The exact condition is 'hits at least one index that is 0 mod 64', not density alone.

- probe_4/5: extra_records=135, seal_sampled_balls=17124, declared_support_checks=17123. So exactly 1 sampled extended shell, against 135/64 ≈ 2.1 expected.

- The comment at full_ball_tower.hpp:199-202 and PROVENANCE.md:2339 and 2350 state the catch without its condition.

Why the severity stays low:
- In practice nothing is exposed. The catalogue is moved const into the seal, which binds the index instance and the storage pointer (:575-577).

- Say 'a fault that hits at least one ball of index 0 mod 64, e.g. one hitting all regular balls with interiors', and add the gap between isolated and dense faults to the declared residual.

findings.title: Early q2 census checks the q2 side's representative, not the merge's
findings.scenario: Under q2_early_census, arity-2 groups take census_key results computed on the smallest q2-slot presentation (q2_representatives), never on groups[g]. If a non-q2 slot ever contributed a smaller arity-2 presentation whose support does not match its key, the post-merge census would refuse it (key mismatch, or shell differs from support) while the early path would accept it silently, breaking the 'same bytes, same refusals' claim. This cannot happen today: GPU lanes emit arity 3 or 4 (lanes.hpp:601, q4_lanes.hpp:634), and the engine emits q3/q4 candidates.
findings.evidence: q2_representatives (952-1011) reads q2_slots only; split_groups (1089-1115) classifies groups by the arity of the merge representative; the only cross-check is key equality (1841). A one-line structural guard would close it: no arity-2 presentation outside the q2 slots, or the merge representative pointer equals the q2-side representative.

votes.corrected_severity: info (a hardening note, not a defect)
votes.reasoning:
Checked at f44a8db03. The finding reads the code correctly. q2_representatives (tower_chain.cpp:958-1011) reads only q2_slots. split_groups (:1089-1115) sorts groups by the arity of the merge representative. The only cross-checks are the key count (:1833) and per-key equality (:1840). Nothing asserts that the merge representative and the q2-side representative are the same presentation. But the scenario cannot happen in the code as written, and the finding admits this ("This cannot happen today"):
- Every q34 engine producer builds candidates with a literal arity of 3 or 4: q34_cover.cpp:310,372; q34_seed.cpp:91,124; q4_window.cpp:93; q4_shallow.cpp:131; q4_local.cpp:456; wspd_q34.cpp:750. The CPU lane records copy that arity (wspd_q34.cpp:1210).
- GPU records are forced to 3, 4 or 0 at tower_chain.cpp:482. Even a corrupted device record cannot enter a non-q2 slot as arity 2, and arity 0 is refused at the merge (:1759, chain_presentation_arity).
- The only other entry point is the test seam (:1712-1732). It forges into slots.front() after the early census has run. But the seam gate (tests/chain/sealed_catalogue_gate.cpp:239-262) forges only arities 3, 4, 5 and 1 and never turns on q2_early_census, which is false by default (tower_chain.hpp:191). The early-census gate is not built with the seam (CMakeLists.txt:489-506).

The doc claims are true of the current code: the comment at :952-954 ("the merge's representative too, arity 2 being the smallest") and PROVENANCE.md:889-891 and :905-908. So there is no false documentation, only an assumption that no check enforces.

The stated consequence is also partly misstated:
1. For arity 2, "shell differs from support" is not a separate refusal. census_key recomputes the key from the support and requires it to equal rep.key (:865). Both ends of a diameter lie exactly on the ball's sphere, so a support whose key matches is contained in the shell, and a shell of size 2 equals it. The only refusals that can differ are a support/key mismatch or an out-of-range ID.
2. If two well-formed arity-2 presentations of the same key are both present, census_key gives the same bytes from either one. The level comes from the key; the regular branch requires shell == support; the extended branch ignores the support. So the "same bytes" claim still holds.
3. In the hypothetical, the harm is a producer fault that goes undetected. The published ball would still be correct, because it comes from the valid q2 presentation. This is not a wrong object.
4. The reference path has the same blind spot for every non-representative presentation. The merge checks only depth and shell agreement and duplicates (:628-634), never key against support, despite the comment "the merge checks every presentation" (:957). The lever changes only which presentation per key gets checked.

A cheap reproduction is not possible. Reaching the case needs a source change: the seam computes forged keys from their supports (:1720-1723), so it can never produce the silent case. The only seam divergence would be a malformed arity-2 forgery with a zero key, which hits a typed refusal (chain_q2_early_census_keys_differ) rather than a silent acceptance. No gate exercises it. I built nothing.

The proposed one-line guard (merge representative == q2-side representative, or no arity-2 presentation outside the q2 slots) is a reasonable defensive assertion. It closes no reachable defect.

result.summary:
I found no data race, no change to the computed object and no error in failure priority. Five low findings are below: two documentation, two gate coverage, one performance attribution.

What I checked and found sound:
- **No shared mutable state during the overlap.** The q2 thread writes only `early`, `q2_slots`, its own members of `result`, and the q2 timestamps. The main thread reads them only after the join, on every path; `Q2Joiner` is declared after all the objects the thread references. The shared helpers do not interfere: `current_pool` is thread_local, `spawned_threads` is only read by the tower after the census, and the failpoints and mutant registry are read-only during a run.
- **The early representative gives the same result as the merge's.** The merge refuses arity 0 or 1 before any early result is read. After that, every q2 key has an arity-2 representative, so the arity-2 groups are exactly the q2-side keys, in the same order. The `split_groups` offsets are correct. Even a different arity-2 support for the same key cannot change the output: two distinct diametral pairs force a shell of at least 3 sites, so the key takes the extended path, whose result depends only on the key; the level depends only on the radius.
- **The error returned is always the smallest failing key.** Every index below the returned one is processed. `early_failed = q2_groups[e]`, the late census stops below it, and the two errors are compared with a min, so it is the smallest key at any W. q2, q34 and merge failures still come first. After the join, the early results are read only if q34 succeeded, the merge passed and the size check held.
- **The cancel flag is safe.** `ready` is read after the loop, with coherence through the join.
- **Moving the tower index out of `early` is safe.** It holds only vectors.
- **No double counting.** Statistics are summed over the two disjoint sets of keys, and nothing is published on failure.
- **R22 used the early census on every lever arm.** In all 24 arms with the lever, `early_census_keys` equals `by_qmin[0]` (no fallback), `q2_census_wait` is 0 and q34 time is unchanged (482-485 vs 488 ms at K5).

findings.title: An allocation failure inside the q2-side census is kept as a key refusal, not sent to the fallback the doc promises
findings.scenario: K10 frame with the pinned pool (1.28 GB), the q34 buffers and early.balls (about 580 MB on raw frames) all alive during the device window. A std::bad_alloc is raised in census_key for q2 key j (growth of st.in/st.sh, LocalCensus push_back, or ShellTable::prepare). parallel_for_first_error records it as early.error at rank j and ready stays true. After the merge it is rethrown as the census error, so the chain ends chain_allocation_failed (resource_exhausted). The fallback census after the merge, once the q34 transient memory is gone, is never tried.
findings.evidence: PROVENANCE.md:921-924 says any other failure on the q2 side ('index, tri, allocation') makes the full census rerun after the merge. In the code, the catch-all at tower_chain.cpp:757-771 captures every exception thrown by the job at 1049-1055 as that key's error. ready is set at 1061 and the error is rethrown at 1864 and 1870. Only exceptions outside the per-key loop reach the fallback catch at 1062. The --fallback gate tests only bad_alloc thrown after the loop (1056-1059). The pre-v28 comment 'the job must throw only according to its data' was dropped. Fix: either say in the doc that per-key allocation failures are refusals, or turn non-Failure exceptions from the early job into a fallback.

votes.corrected_severity: informational (wording only), if kept at all
votes.reasoning:
Checked at f44a8db03. The finding describes the code correctly but misreads the doc, so there is no contradiction between them.

What the code does (as the finding says): tower_chain.cpp:757-771 catches every exception the per-key job throws. The job at 1049-1055 therefore keeps a std::bad_alloc from census_key at its key rank as early.error. `ready` is set at 1061. The error comes back through census_error (1856-1857) and is rethrown at 1870. The catch at 1997 then gives resource_exhausted / chain_allocation_failed.

Why this is not a contradiction with the doc:
1. PROVENANCE.md sorts failures by where they happen, not by exception type. Line 918 says "un échec du census côté q2 garde son rang de clé". An allocation failure inside census_key is a census failure on the q2 side, so this bullet covers it. Line 921 says "tout autre échec du côté q2 (index, tri, allocation)", and "autre" means failures outside the per-key census: build_tower_index, q2_representatives, and the resize/assign of early.balls, keep and states at 1045-1047.
2. Everything else in the code base uses the same split. The struct comment at tower_chain.cpp:1016-1021 says `ready` is set "only if the part completed outside the per-key census (a census failure is kept with its rank for the merge); any other exception leaves it unset". The header (tower_chain.hpp:440-442) and the gate doc (chain_q2_early_census_gate.cpp:27-29 and 382-385) both define the fallback as "une panne hors du census clé par clé". The --fallback gate's std::bad_alloc failpoint (kEarlyAfterCensus, thrown after the loop) is exactly the "allocation" example the doc gives.
3. The doc never promises a retry once q34 memory is freed. The fallback exists to put a deterministic failure back at its place in the chain: the doc says it "rencontre alors le même échec". It is not meant to relieve memory pressure.
4. Nothing changed for this case. Before v28, parallel_for also rethrew a bad_alloc from a key's census, which ended as chain_allocation_failed. The census after the merge (1816-1826) still does the same. The pre-v28 comment "Le job ne doit lever que selon ses données (jamais selon l'ordre des fils)" was about the result not depending on thread order. It lives on as "A key's refusal depends on its data alone" at 1812, so it was not dropped.
5. The practical effect is negligible. The lever's extra memory is documented (about 580 MB at K10 raw, PROVENANCE memory bullet). The pinned pool (1.28 GB) plus early.balls is small against a g4-standard-48 host's RAM. Under Linux overcommit, operator new rarely throws in any case. Even if it did, the result is an honest transactional refusal (resource_exhausted), not a wrong or partly published result.

At most, the "(index, tri, allocation)" in the doc could say "hors du census clé par clé" to remove any ambiguity. That is informational only.

findings.title: Test seam is absent on the q2 side; the keys_differ and key_mismatch refusals have no negative fixture

votes.corrected_severity: low (informational test-coverage gap; the lane-record arm is refuted)
votes.reasoning:
The core claim holds at f44a8db03, but one arm of the evidence is wrong. I built nothing: the code reading settles it and the host is loaded.

What holds:
- **Seam placement.** The census_delay_group / census_faults seam sits only in the fallback loop (tower_chain.cpp:1817-1823, the `!early_ready` branch) and in the late-groups loop (1854-1860). Under `early_ready`, the q2 groups are copied from early.balls/early.keep at 1836-1844 with no seam. `run_early_census` (1034-1048) has no seam either. A planted fault or delay on a q2 group is therefore skipped when q2_early_census is on. Commit f6e48cd8a's "the seal gate's test seam sits in both census loops" does refer to those two post-merge loops.
- **Forged presentations.** They are appended after the q2 slots join (1706-1732), so after the early census has taken its representatives. A forged arity-2 key that q2 did not emit makes q2_groups one larger than early.balls. Under the lever the chain refuses with chain_q2_early_census_keys_differ (1833). Without the lever, census_key judges that key with its own reason. The same happens for a malformed arity-2 forgery (zero key): keys_differ instead of the typed refusal.
- **No fixture and no gate combining the two.** The two reason strings appear only at 1833/1845 and in PROVENANCE.md:907. None of tests/, bench/, gcp-migration/ or CMakeLists.txt has them. The seal gate's options_for (sealed_catalogue_gate.cpp:202-209) never sets q2_during_device or q2_early_census. The early-census gate is built with MHGP9_TESTING only (CMakeLists.txt:49-51, 486-495), never with MHGP9_CHAIN_TEST_SEAM, and its failpoints fire inside census_key, so they land in early.error, not in keys_differ. So deleting either require survives every gate. That is latent, as the finding says.
- **An extra point in the finding's favour.** Suppose keys_differ is deleted and the extra arity-2 group has a key above every q2 key. Key_mismatch never sees it, because the loop reads only the first `taken` entries. The group is neither taken nor in late_groups, so it keeps keep=0 and the ball drops out of the catalogue silently. The guard matters; it just has no test.

What is wrong or overstated:
- **Lane records with arity 2 cannot reach the sink.** "The lanes sink copies r.arity without a check (1485); on G4 only the worker identity q2_accepted_pairs == q2_presentations would catch an arity-2 lane record" is false. lanes_batch, on both the device and the host-emulation path, clamps any arity outside {3,4} to 0 (tower_chain.cpp:482). check_lanes_batch then throws before any sink call on a record whose arity is not 3 or 4 with a valid shape (wspd_q34.cpp:1296-1308, called at 1764; sink at 1821). An arity-0 presentation would in any case be refused at the merge by chain_presentation_arity (tower_chain.cpp:1745).
- **Test-only reach.** The remaining unchecked arity source, the engine consumer (1409-1417), emits q3/q4 by construction. Every other trigger for these refusals needs the test-only seam, which the product build does not compile.
- **Consequences are milder than stated.** In (b) the lever changes only the refusal reason; both arms still refuse with invariant_violated. In (a) the fault is "silently skipped" by the seam, but any gate that checks the expected reason (census_order does, at sealed_catalogue_gate.cpp:361-363) would fail loudly on a complete result. It is a composition hazard in the test harness, not a silent hole in the product.

Prior audits: no earlier A/B/C audit covers these two refusals or the seam/lever pairing. The lever (f6e48cd8a) postdates C's R21 counter-read (488bcef11), and neither CONTRE_AUDIT_C_R21 nor ETAT_COURANT mentions it. The class, however, was already raised by C in finding L4-03 of the 23 September grand audit (audits/c_audit_20260923/verifications/verdicts.json, around lines 905-935). That finding covered the chain's cross-check guards having no causal gate, and asked for compiled chain mutants (for example "arity 3 on a q2 key", "altered key"). This finding is a new instance of that class for the two v28 requires.

A cheap fix, if wanted: under MHGP9_CHAIN_TEST_SEAM, enable the lever in one seal-gate case. Plant a forged arity-2 pair whose key is above every q2 key, expecting keys_differ, and one whose key lies inside the q2 range, which keys_differ would also catch. Then a require-deletion mutant for each; with keys_differ deleted, the in-range forgery should be caught by key_mismatch.

What is overstated or misstated:
(a) "Silent" is too strong. Each `vm/probe_N.stdout` is kept in the receipt and hashed in SHA256SUMS, and a fallback shows there as `early_census_keys=0` with `tower_index_ms>0`. It is silent only in the worker verdict and in SUMMARY.

result.summary:
The object is not at risk. The findings are about cost attribution, device paths that never ran, and telemetry.

**What is correct:**
- **Lease lifetime:** the lease sits in the local `out` of lanes_batch and is released after the conversion (tower_chain.cpp:464-487). refused() drops it (filter_runner.cu:1202-1210, 1442-1450).
- **Copy in flight:** cudaMemcpy D2H is synchronous, so no copy can still be running when a block is reused.
- **Growth:** a leased block is never grown or freed. Growth only replaces the memory of a free block, and it is allocated before it is swapped in (record_pool.hpp:188-250).
- **Locks:** always res.mu first, then the pool mutex. There is no inversion.
- **Stale data:** there is no stale read. The lease holds exactly `used` records. The always-on check_lanes_batch (wspd_q34.cpp:1764) checks slice bounds and that the records are partitioned exactly (:1288-1290, :1323-1340). A short, zeroed or stale copy would be refused at run time.
- **On/off:** the bytes are identical. The 24 R22 comparisons are equal, pinned on and off included. The device pinned path was judged edge by edge in the preflight (28,728 edges) and in preflight_deferral (15,486 decided, 11,993 deferred, so partial batches are covered).
- **Empty batches:** acquire(0) returns an empty lease and record_data() falls back to the empty vector.
- **CPU stub:** it returns no_device, and the chain turns that into a refusal before its path check.
- **TSan:** the pool gate is clean.
- **Timers:** host_alloc is about 0.007 ms. The pageable copy window (e5..e6) dominates and includes page first-touch. filter_runner.hpp:333-356 documents this honestly.

**Main issues:**
1. The chain-wall gain moves cost outside chain_total. Per single-frame process (all R22 probes), the lever is neutral at K5 and a loss at K10.
2. None of the device-only paths ran on G4: stage B allocating the pool, growth inside the call window, and the device gates that PROVENANCE requires before any credit.
3. lanes_pinned_reserve_records reports the requested count, not what was actually reserved.
4. No gate can see a lease returned too early.

Minor, not listed as a finding: in lanes_host.hpp:88-103 the before/after stats on the process-wide host pool are not atomic, so concurrent host-twin calls could misattribute pinned_allocations (telemetry only).

findings.title: The pinned gain moves cost outside chain_total: per single-frame process it is neutral at K5 and a loss at K10
findings.scenario: Pinned-only ablation at 08/000000 (arms with and without the pool, all else the same). K10: chain_total 2961/2994 ms with the pool against 3121 ms without, a 127-160 ms gain. But the process's external wall is 6.029/6.036 s with the pool against 5.885 s without, so 144-151 ms longer. Two costs explain it. First, the device session pays the pool reservation (190-192 ms, outside chain_total). Second, the time outside any timer (external wall minus every published timer) is 364-374 ms with the pool against 285-291 ms without, about +80 ms; this is most likely the unpinning of the leaked 1.28 GB pool at process exit. K5: 1.718/1.772 s with the pool against 1.725 s without. The README credits the three levers with -62..-82 / -224..-266 ms and a records copy divided by 14 without netting these costs. The gain only exists in a resident process that serves 2-3 or more frames per reservation, and no case measures more than one frame per process. The pinned block is also fully resident and locked whatever the frame uses: at K10 without ground, 4.63 M of 10 M records are used, yet RSS rises by 1.05-1.29 GB (6.34-6.36 GB against 5.21 GB).

votes.reasoning:
I re-derived the numbers from the receipt at f44a8db03 (vm/probe_*.command.json, stdout, and the /usr/bin/time -v stderr). All of the finding's timings reproduce.

Arms at 08/000000, identified from argv:
- K10: all three levers are probes 2 and 15; without the pool is 23; gpu_r21 is 14 and 17; without the seal is 19; without early census is 21.
- K5: the same arms are 0 and 13, then 22, then 12 and 16, then 18, then 20.

What the numbers show:
- **K10 with the pool against without it** (probes 2/15 vs 23):
  - The chain gets faster by 127 to 159 ms (2961/2994 vs 3121).
  - The external wall gets longer by 144 to 151 ms (6.029/6.036 vs 5.885 s).
  - The session reservation adds 190.2/191.9 ms.
- **Time outside every published timer.** This is elapsed minus read, prepare, chain_total, digest, catalogue_digest, context_ms, reserve_ms and pinned_ms.
  - Every arm with the pool (2, 15, 19, 21) shows 363 to 373 ms.
  - Every arm without it (23, 14, 17) shows 284 to 290 ms.
  - The two groups do not overlap, so about +80 ms goes with the pool.
  - Blaming it on releasing the leaked pool at exit is plausible but not proven. The code does leak the pool: record_pool.hpp:40-42, filter_runner.cu:1163, PROVENANCE.md:1426. Either way the cost belongs to the pool.
- **K5** (probes 0/13 vs 22): 1.718/1.772 s against 1.725 s, so neutral within noise. The outside time rises about +20 ms, which fits a 256 MB pool.
- **All three levers against gpu_r21 at K10**: the external wall is also 37 to 49 ms longer (6.03 vs 5.99 s). So for a one-frame process, the three levers together are a small net loss at K10 too.
- **Code**:
  - The reservation sits outside the chain. filter_runner.cu:1507-1522 does it, and tower_probe.cpp:229-233 opens the session before run_tower_chain.
  - The pool size is fixed by order, not by what the frame uses: filter_runner.hpp:270-272 gives 10 M records at K10, while the frame uses 4,630,767.
- **RSS**: 6.34 to 6.44 GB against 5.21 GB without the pool. That is +1.13 to 1.23 GB, not the finding's "1.05-1.29 (6.34-6.36)"; the error is small.

Why the finding is overstated:
- **The design is one session per process.** PROVENANCE.md:1310-1312 says the setup cost is paid once per process, and that a 10 Hz LiDAR stream opens it at startup, not on every frame. The pool reservation is in the same bucket as the CUDA context: 121 to 166 ms per process, also outside chain_total, and C's R21 counter-audit accepted that convention.
- **The README does declare the reservation cost** next to the gains: 38-40 ms at K5 and 190-201 ms at K10 (README.md:74-76). It also counts the 1.28 GB pool in the RSS peak (README.md:104-105). The lever claims at README.md:100-103 are stated for the chain, which is the receipt's metric throughout.
- **The per-frame gain should hold in a resident process.** Without the pool, every call copies into a fresh pageable vector and pays the first touch again (record_pool.hpp:6-12). With the pool, the block is already reserved and reused. The "divided by 14" copy figure (144.9 down to 10.5 ms) is correct.

What survives:
- The roughly 80 ms exit teardown at K10 (about 20 ms at K5) is not declared anywhere.
- Amortisation over several frames is assumed but never measured: the probe serves one frame per process.
- About 1.1 GB stays resident whatever the frame uses.
- The claim "loss per single-frame process" is true, but that is not the deployment model.

Earlier audits: none raised this. The pool is new in R22, and C's R21 counter-audit recommended pinned D2H without discussing netting it. findings.title: No gate can see a lease returned before the conversion
findings.scenario: A chain makes a single lanes call, and the pool never frees or overwrites a returned block. So a regression that returns the lease before parallel_ranges survives every gate and G4: for example 'out.pinned.reset()' after taking record_data(), or moving the lease into a temporary that dies first. The conversion still reads intact bytes. The four pool mutants and PINNED_READS_VECTOR do not cover this. It would only corrupt data once a concurrent or second lanes call takes the freed block, which is exactly the 'a concurrent lease takes another block' contract that record_pool.hpp:15-19 advertises for future multi-frame pipelining. Fix: poison a block when it is returned (test build, host twin) and add a mutant that returns the lease early.
findings.evidence: tower_chain.cpp:458-487 (records read through a raw pointer while `out` holds the lease); record_pool.hpp:252-255 (give_back only clears the leased flag); CMakeLists.txt mutant list: TAKE_LEASED, NO_RETURN, KEEP_TAKEN_ON_THROW, PINNED_SHORT_COPY, CHAIN_MUTANT_PINNED_READS_VECTOR (none returns early).

votes.corrected_severity: low (a test-hardening gap, no current defect)
votes.reasoning:
I could not refute the gate gap. The code at f44a8db03 is correct as written, and no gate would catch the regression the finding describes.

Code as written is correct:
- In lanes_batch, `out` lives in function scope from tower_chain.cpp:427 to the return at :539.
- The raw pointer and count are taken at :463-464 and read inside parallel_ranges at :471-487, so the lease outlives the conversion.

Why an early return would not be seen:
1. **Only the flag is cleared.** Lease::reset -> give_back (record_pool.hpp:113-122, :252-255) clears the leased flag and touches no memory. A block's memory is only released when a later take() grows it (:239-248).
2. **One lanes call per chain.** There is a single run_lanes_batch call site (tower_chain.cpp:427). It is invoked once, in phase 2c of run_wspd_q34_batched (wspd_q34.cpp:1681-1714). tower_probe runs one chain per process (bench/tower_probe.cpp:233).
3. **The pinned gate runs its chains one after another.** pinned_gate (tests/chain/chain_batch_q3_gate.cpp:79-150) calls run_tower_chain in sequence. A block returned early is only reacquired by the next chain, after the conversion has finished.
4. **The count checks miss a reset placed after the capture.** A reset *before* :463 would make record_data()/record_total() fall back to the empty vector (filter_runner.hpp:373-374). The gate would then fail at pinned.records. A reset *after* :464 keeps the captured pointer and total, so every digest and count stays equal.
5. **ASan cannot see it either,** since nothing is freed within one chain.
6. **No existing mutant covers it.** The mutant list (CMakeLists.txt:539, :652-667) is TAKE_LEASED, NO_RETURN, KEEP_TAKEN_ON_THROW, PINNED_SHORT_COPY and PINNED_READS_VECTOR. pinned.resident (:142) catches a lease that is *never* returned, not one returned early.

Pool-only reproduction: scratchpad/r22/verify_rev-pinned_3_0/early_return.cpp, built against the repository's record_pool.hpp. Output:
```
single_call_after_early_return intact=1
second_lease_same_block=1
reader_sees_corruption=1
reserve_grew=1 old_block_freed=1
```
- After an early reset, a single call still reads intact bytes.
- A second acquire gets the same block and overwrites what the reader sees.
- A larger reserve grows the free block and releases the old memory.

One precision on the consequence, which does not weaken the finding. On the device, a second actor already exists inside one chain, not only in future multi-frame pipelining. Stage B's warm_up_lanes -> res.pinned.reserve(pinned_records_for_order(k)) (filter_runner.cu:1454-1476, tower_chain.cpp:171-177) is "never waited for". If it lost the race for res.mu to the lanes call, it would grow a returned block smaller than 2M/10M records. That would release pinned memory while the conversion still reads it. In practice stage B runs well before the lanes call, because the filter and certificate calls come first. So this path is theoretical and gates cannot exercise it reliably.

Severity is low: the code has no defect today, and this is a missing guard against a plausible regression. The proposed fix is sound: poison the block on give_back in the host twin under a test define, and add a chain mutant that resets `out.pinned` after :464. chain_batch_q3_gate --pinned would then catch it through its digest comparison.

I could not refute it. I checked by reading the code at f44a8db03 and did not build; the claim rests on reachability, not on a run.

**No gate can reach the helper-launch catch**
- `full_ball_tower.hpp:985-1008`: `std::vector<std::thread> helper;` has no reserve and no failpoint before `helper.emplace_back`. The catch at 1003 writes `population_errors[i]`.
- The MHGP9_TESTING failpoints (280-345) have no hook for this launch. `failpoint_runner_launch` is called only for runners (945).
- `parallel_detail::launch_fail_after` is thread_local (`pool.hpp:62`). It is checked only in the TaskPool and per-call launch loops (`pool.hpp:131`, `pool.hpp:339`).
- The gates that override `operator new` or set rlimits do not include `full_ball_tower.hpp` or `tower_chain.hpp`.
- The unwind gate covers static_alloc/launch, rows and images_alloc only (`order_failure_priority_gate.cpp:76-82`, `:118-121`, `:150-153`).
- So the new behaviour of f9471b4de (drop the `return`, phase C still runs) has no test, and a revert survives every gate. The "eighteen checks" in the commit message are the `images_alloc` cases, not helper launch.

**What a revert would change is stated correctly, but it needs three faults, not two**
- After the join, `population_errors` are rethrown only when no lot has failed (1076-1078). Image errors are rethrown only for `i < imaged` (1079-1086). Then Failures are taken by (K, lots, populations, images) (1095-1099).
- A revert is visible only when all three happen together:
  - the helper for order K fails to launch;
  - a lot Failure occurs at some K' > K, so the population error is dropped;
  - order K's images fail, with a Failure or another exception.
- The witness runs the images for `i < lots_done` (1103-1117, `populations_done` at 858-864), so it reports images of K. The reverted code skips phase C of K and reports lots of K'.
- With one fault (the launch failure) or two, both versions report the same thing.

**The overwrite is real and needs two faults**
- On runner 0, a failed rows sizing stores `bad_alloc` in `population_errors[0]` (963-969).
- A later helper-launch `system_error` overwrites it at 1003. No other writer races on that slot: the helper, when it launches, returns at once because `rows != 1`.
- The two exceptions map to `full_ball_allocation_failed` and `full_ball_thread_launch_failed`, both `kResourceExhausted` (3051-3059).
- If the vector allocation itself throws `bad_alloc`, the reason does not change.
- This overwrite was not introduced by f9471b4de. It dates from v28 (a70ad6c7a), which moved the rows error into `population_errors[0]`; the old catch with `return` already overwrote that slot.

- It happens only on refusal paths, and `orders` are cleared (3061). No wrong tower and no partial payload is published.
- Only the refusal reason can differ, and only under compound faults, at least one of them environmental.

I could not refute the finding. The gap is real, but it only affects scheduling metadata, and C already raised it once.

**The code at f44a8db03**
- `runner_threads` is only ever incremented inside `run_orders_overlapped` (full_ball_tower.hpp:1021). That function is reached only when `geometry_threads>1 && kmax>1 && !batch_resolver.resolve` (line 631) and `overlap_static_lots` (line 791). With overlap off, the real code always reports `runner_threads=0`.
- The worker checks `runner_threads` only under `static_path and tower_overlap_static` (tower_worker_v9.py:907).
- `helper_threads` goes through `_count` alone (line 885, i.e. below 2^64). No value rule applies to it.
- `pool_jobs` is constrained only by `(pool_jobs>0)==pooled` (line 909). It has no upper bound, and 1 is still accepted.
- The selftest fake emits `runner_threads=effective if static_path` whatever the overlap lever says (tower_selftest_v9.py:291).

**Reproduction.** I copied C's probe_reader_gaps.py to scratchpad/r22/verify_fixcheck_3_0/ and ran it against the repository without changing anything. The output:
- `overlap off baseline complete_relative runner_threads= 5`
- `overlap off runner_threads=1e9 -> complete_relative`
- `helper_threads=2**63 -> complete_relative`
- `pool_jobs=2**63 -> complete_relative`

**Where the finding overstates**
1. **Consequence.** These counters are path and scheduling metadata, "never part of tower_work" (full_ball_tower.hpp:82-91). The object itself is still judged by the pinned digests. In R22, all 36 probes run with overlap on, and every one shows `runner_threads==K`, `hashed_orders==K-1`, `pool_jobs` of 45 (K5) or 80 (K10) and `helper_threads` between 406 and 912. No R22 conclusion is affected. A plan with overlap off is admissible, but only outside the first case (line 449), so the gap is latent.
2. **"The selftest fake passes".** The selftest never runs an overlap-off case on the static path. Its mixed cases switch off only pipelined_tail, hash_grouping, persistent_pool and sealed_catalogue (around tower_selftest_v9.py:1190). `tower_overlap_static=False` appears only as a lever-mismatch mutation, which is refused (line 1258). The fake's wrong branch shows up only in C's probe.
3. **hashed_orders == K-1.** This is not a defect.
   - The fallback (full_ball_tower.hpp:2602-2603) also needs a bound `batch_resolver`. No production or probe code binds one: `FullBallBatchResolver` has no user outside full_ball_tower.hpp.
   - The plan domain is whole frames of at most about 126k sites with K in {5,10}. The largest K10 case has 5.5M balls and 4.5M contributions, orders of magnitude below 2^31 requests.
   - If the fallback were ever reached, the rule would refuse a legitimate run, which fails safe. At most, the comment could mention it.
   - C's original finding 11 named this same fallback, judged it unreachable, and recommended exactly this equality. Its skeptic vote agreed.
4. **helper_threads.** A tight rule is not natural here. B noted that it is a process-wide delta, exact only when nothing else uses the helpers at the same time (CONTRE_AUDIT_B_POOL_E2_WIP_20260924.md:59). Only an upper bound could be derived.

**Earlier audits.** This is not new. C's finding 11 (CONTRE_AUDIT_C_R21_TOUR_INTEGREE_20260926.md:338, which recommends "bornes sur les autres") already said, per the annex c_r21_20260926/lanes_results.json:416-417:
- "helper_threads and runner_threads are never checked, even under the witness arm"
- pool_jobs=1 and helper_threads=10^9 are accepted.

The developer's closure note ("10 à 12 : bornes, égalités et cas mixtes du lecteur", audits/COORDINATION_MORSEHGP3D_V9.md, 01 h 33 entry) added only `runner_threads==K` on the overlapped path and the bound on deferred refs. Finding 11 is therefore only partly closed:
- `runner_threads==0` off the overlapped path is still missing.
- `helper_threads` and `pool_jobs` still have no value rule or upper bound.

findings.title: Review-before-R22 additions without negative tests: preflight lever rules and the pinned flag's empty-call clause
findings.scenario: The three new validate_preflight_work clauses (early census with no fallback, seal, pinned pool; 1113-1116) have no selftest mutation. Removing the early-census clause, the only one not implied by validate_probe, would let a preflight that fell back to the tower-side census pass. The sealed clause is redundant with validate_tower_detail (sealed_catalogues == 1 under the lever). In C++, `steps.pinned = out.pinned_records && !where.empty()` (tower_chain.cpp:535) is not exercised by any gate with an empty lanes call under q34_lanes_pinned. A regression would only cause a false reader refusal.
findings.evidence: grep finds no validate_preflight_work test in tower_selftest_v9.py; the vacuous_preflight fake (tower_selftest_v9.py:335-337) zeroes only q3/q4. chain_batch_q3_gate.cpp:96-145 checks pinned only with records present. votes.corrected_severity: low (test-coverage hygiene; no effect on the object or on R22's published result)
votes.reasoning:
The finding holds as written at f44a8db03, but its impact is very small.

1) The clauses exist and are new. gcp-migration/tower_worker_v9.py:1113-1116 was added in f9471b4de ("review before r22 ... The preflight must exercise the q2 early census (no fallback), the seal and the pinned pool"). That commit came after C's R21 counter-read (488bcef11). I grepped audits/ for validate_preflight_work, where.empty and preflight+early and got no hits, so no earlier audit (A, B or C) raised this.

2) No test mutates these clauses. The fake probe in tower_selftest_v9.py has only these preflight modifiers: fail_preflight, vacuous_preflight, vacuous_engine_preflight, preflight_batch_differs and deferral_differs (lines 327-339).
- vacuous_preflight zeroes q3/q4 emitted and presented, so it trips the first need at worker:1093.
- vacuous_engine_preflight trips the leaf-census clause.
- The v28 mutants at selftest:1124-1144 ('sealed catalogue flag dropped', 'early census keys shifted' =2, 'pinned lanes flag dropped') go through validate_probe on case values. None of them sets early_census_keys=0 on the preflight.
- No other Python test calls validate_preflight_work. tower_session_v9.py:268 calls it again on the host, which is still untested.

3) Which clauses are redundant:
- **Sealed:** redundant. validate_tower_detail (worker:916-917) already requires sealed_catalogues == 1 under the lever.
- **Pinned:** also implied. q34_lanes_pinned requires q34_batch_q3 (worker:405). The preflight's own clause requires lanes_decided > 0 (worker:1105). lanes_decided + lanes_deferred == lanes_asked (worker:762), so ran_call is true. validate_lanes then requires lanes_pinned == True (worker:743-744).
- **Early census:** the only substantive clause. validate_probe accepts early_census_keys in (0, by_qmin[0]) under the lever (worker:992-999), so a preflight that fell back to the tower-side census passes if 1113-1114 is removed or weakened.

4) Direct-call reproduction (scratchpad/r22/verify_fixcheck_5_0/check.py, importing the worktree module read-only). A minimal value passing every other clause is ACCEPTED. It is REFUSED with early_census_keys=0, with sealed_catalogues=0 and with lanes_pinned=False. So the rules work but nothing guards them.

5) C++ side: `steps.pinned = out.pinned_records && !where.empty()` is at tower_chain.cpp:535. chain_batch_q3_gate.cpp:127-131 requires lanes_pinned on every pinned case, and the gate passes. So every case has lanes_asked > 0 and the empty-call branch is never exercised. The finding says "only with records present"; strictly the condition is asked edges, but the point stands. A regression there would only make the reader at worker:744 refuse a valid run, as the finding says.

6) Why the severity is low:
- probe_worker_contract.py:166-173 (real probe, r22_on case) already checks on the C++ side that early_census_keys == by_qmin[0] > 0, lanes_pinned is True and sealed_catalogues == 1. For a fallback preflight to pass unnoticed, both the Python clause would have to regress and the probe would have to fall back only on the preflight cloud.
- A fallback is still a correct object. It only means the preflight no longer proves that the early-census path ran, which affects timing attribution.
- The R22 receipt's preflight exercised all three levers: vm/preflight.stdout has early_census_keys=22458 == by_qmin[0], sealed_catalogues=1, lanes_pinned=True and lanes_asked=28728.

The gap is real only against the project's own doctrine that every gate gets a killed mutant. A cheap fix is one selftest mutant setting early_census_keys=0 on the preflight.
